Ethos & Vision
Through God We Achieve
‘”Turning your ear to wisdom and applying your heart to understanding”
Our Vision
To deliver outstanding education in a caring community, with God at its centre.
Our Values
Joy – We provide a happy and stimulating environment, rooted in Christian values.
Excellence – we are a church school committed to the highest standards in everything we do.
Relationship – we work hand in hand with our parents and carers, St Stephen’s Church and the community.
Respect – we enable our children to deepen or realise their own faith and respect the freedom of others in their beliefs.
Nurture – our children are cared for spiritually, morally, intellectually, physically, socially and emotionally.

Headmaster’s Welcome
I am delighted that you are considering St. Stephen’s CE Primary School for your child’s education. We have been serving the local community for over 160 years. St Stephen’s was part of the original village of Shepherd’s Bush and built at the same time as the Church. This is a marvellous area that is culturally varied and has great access to the riches of galleries, museums and theatres in central London.
At St. Stephen’s, we actively seek to develop a creative curriculum; giving each child a balanced education involving the Arts and The National Curriculum. I strongly believe that every child has a unique skill or quality – and it is our responsibility to nurture that potential by offering a wide range of opportunities to develop and enhance it. We provide a rich and diverse curriculum and our aim is to shape happy and inspired children who are ready for our world.
As well as a focused and successful learning programme that looks at children’s individual needs, St Stephen’s provides a lively and diverse after school club programme, educational trips in and around London, a range of residential trips for children from Year 2 upwards, many different sporting activities, individual music tuition and the opportunity to take part in a range of performances both in and out of school.
The School community is also committed to fundraising for additional resources to enhance our children’s educational experience. The Friends of St Stephen’s (FoSS) run many fundraising and social events throughout the year. All parents of St Stephen’s become members of the FoSS on joining the school and the committee welcome any parents/carers who wish to join in to help with the organisation of these events.
At St Stephen’s, we see parents as valuable partners in the education and welfare of the children, and we encourage their involvement in the school community. Often the first contact we have with parents is during a pre-school visit prior to a child starting in the school. From this initial contact, we hope to build a strong partnership between parents and teachers. There are many ways in which parents can become involved: hearing children read, the school production, sewing, the school library, photocopying, art work and playing educational games with groups of children – and much more.
At Stephen’s CE Primary School, we are committed to providing an outstanding education in a caring community with God at its centre, which celebrates the diversity of the local area.
Mr Schumm – Headteacher
Assistant Headteacher
Sally Bouwman – Assistant Head – SENCo / Inclusion
I have over 30 years’ experience working in primary and some secondary school settings. I have always had a particular interest in children who may find school based learning challenging at times. I am a trained Reading Recovery teacher, have the OCR level 7 Diploma in SpLD/dyslexia. I am passionate about creating good inclusive practice in our classrooms, working with all the staff and parents and carers to better serve the needs of our children. I am committed to ensuring that our children have access to a full and interesting curriculum and that it reflects the diversity of our school and it’s wider community. I work closely with teachers to develop and support learning across all areas of teaching and learning, as well as supporting the Headteacher as part of the Senior Leadership Team.

School Hours, Extra Curricular & Club House
School Day
The main school day runs between 8:55am and 3:25pm in EYFS and KS1 and from 8:55am to 3:30pm in KS2.
EYFS (Nursery and Reception classes) start at 8:55am.
From Year 1 up we have a soft start system where the children can come into the classroom anytime from 8:45am as long as they are in before registration at 8:55am.
Children’s school attendance is 32.5 hours a week excluding clubs and extra curricular activities.
Breakfast Club
Breakfast is served only from 7.30 am to 8.20 am, after breakfast the children are escorted to the playground at 8.45 am where a member of staff will be on duty to supervise them until the start of the day. Breakfast usually consists of toast, jam and cereal. The cost of the Breakfast Club is £4.50 per day, fees will be payable in advance, breakfast Club is in the nursery building. The entrance is on Coverdale Road and parents should ring the ‘Breakfast Club’ buzzer to gain entry.
If you have more than one child attending breakfast club, the costs are shown below.
To pay for Breakfast Club online with Parent Mail, please click on the button below:
Club House
We are delighted to offer a wide range of exciting clubs to all the children of St Stephens, Martial Arts, Drama, Football and Tennis to name a few.
The clubs are all very well attended and the children fully enjoy their club experience whether doing Football club or Ballet.
The club Tutors are all qualified and DBS checked.
We currently run approx. six clubs between 4:00 – 5:00 pm per day and many early morning clubs Monday – Wednesday
Club House runs from 3:30 pm – 6:00 pm and is open every school day.
The Club House runs three sessions per day
Children are escorted from their classrooms by their teacher to the main hall (early years/KS1) or playground (KS2).
Upon arrival they have a light healthy snack and then can choose from a range of activities and games available.
Children are offered a variety of activities as part of the Clubhouse experience: puzzles, games, arts and crafts, construction kits.
We also have a new selection of books to browse or chill out with.
We have a very experience staff team who plan activities to reflect various events and celebrations in collaboration with the school.

The school is set up with a number of different childcare voucher agencies including; Edenred, Care-4, Kiddivouchers, ComputerShare Voucher Services and many more. You need to register for these schemes through your workplace.

Music Tuition
Pelican Music is a leading provider of high quality music tuition for young people at all stages of their musical development. We run instrumental lessons, orchestras, choirs, masterclasses, study days, after school clubs and a Saturday School all lead by professional musicians who are passionate about their instrument and music education. Our teaching staff all have a conservatoire training and regularly perform themselves.
We are based at St Stephen’s school and provide a full range of musical opportunities for pupils at St Stephen’s.
We provide one-to-one instrumental lessons in piano, guitar, drums, brass (cornet, trumpet, trombone, euphonium), woodwind (fife, flute, clarinet, saxophone), violin, viola and cello as well as music theory. 20 or 30 minute lessons are taught in school time with 30 lessons spread across the academic year (approx 10 per term).
The Pelican team also run the KS1 and KS2 school orchestras and can offer lessons after school and at weekends – all at St Stephen’s.
We are passionate about performance and regularly arrange concerts and performance opportunities – both in school and as part of external events – for our young players at all stages of their musical development.
Our Saturday Music School is open to all children who play an orchestral instrument with orchestras. Our Young Singers chamber choir is open pupils in years 4-6 by audition.
If you are interested in lessons for your child or would like more information about any of our Pelican Music activities, please do drop us a line at admin@pelican-music.co.uk.

Library News: Autumn Leaves are Falling….
🍂📚 AUTUMN HAS ARRIVED! 🍎🎃
Crunchy leaves, shiny conkers, juicy apples and enormous pumpkins… autumn is here!
“All those golden autumn days the sky was full of wings…”
This beautiful description of autumn comes from Laura Ingalls Wilder, author of the famous Little House on the Prairie series. She was describing birds flying south as the seasons changed.
This week in the library we are celebrating all things autumn! 🍁
We have stories about falling leaves, geese, apples, pumpkins, forests and changing seasons for our Early Years and KS1 children.
We are also looking forward to Family Supper on Thursday and getting ready for our Harvest Festival next week. 🌾🍎
📚 DON’T FORGET YOUR LIBRARY BOOK!
🗓️ Your library days
Year 2, Year 5 & Year 6
Remember to bring your library book with you! 📖
🍁 THIS WEEK’S STORY PICKS
🐿️ RECEPTION
🍂 The Leaf Thief
Squirrel is VERY worried. The leaves are disappearing from the tree! Who could possibly be stealing them?
A funny autumn story perfect for little readers.
🐸 Frog and Toad All Year
Join Frog and Toad as they enjoy adventures throughout the changing seasons.
Can you spot the signs of autumn? 🍁
🪿 YEAR 1
🍁 Little Goose’s Autumn
Little Goose discovers all the wonderful changes that autumn brings.
Look out for falling leaves, chilly weather and autumn colours!
🌳 Tidy
Pete the badger LOVES being tidy. But what happens when he decides that the whole forest needs a tidy-up?
Would you like Pete to tidy YOUR bedroom? 😂
🍎 YEAR 2
🍏 Apple Doll
A lovely autumn story celebrating apples, creativity and family traditions.
🎃 Too Many Pumpkins
Rebecca never wanted pumpkins… but one day her garden becomes completely full of them!
What would YOU do with hundreds of pumpkins? 🎃
🍂 AUTUMN FACT FILE!
🟡 WHY DO LEAVES CHANGE COLOUR?
During summer, leaves are full of a green substance called chlorophyll.
When autumn arrives and there is less sunlight, the green colour fades and we begin to see beautiful yellow, orange and red colours.
🍁 Nature’s very own colour show!
🪿 HOW FAR CAN GEESE FLY?
Some geese travel thousands of miles when they migrate to warmer places.
They often fly in a V shape.
Flying in formation can help the birds save energy on their long journey.
Imagine flying all the way to another country without an aeroplane! ✈️🪿
🎃 IS A PUMPKIN A FRUIT OR A VEGETABLE?
Pumpkins grow from flowers and contain seeds, which means botanically they are fruits.
Pumpkins are related to cucumbers, melons and courgettes.
📚🍁 AUTUMN READING LIST
🌱 EYFS & KS1
🍂 The Leaf Thief – Alice Hemming 🐿️ The Busy Little Squirrel – Nancy Tafuri 🍎 Apple Cake – Dawn Casey 🎃 Too Many Pumpkins – Linda White 🪿 Little Goose’s Autumn – Elli Woollard 🌳 Tidy – Emily Gravett 🐸 Frog and Toad All Year – Arnold Lobel 🍁 Leaf Man – Lois Ehlert 🌰 The Extraordinary Gardener – Sam Boughton 🍂 We’re Going on a Leaf Hunt – Steve Metzger
📖🌳 KS2
🍁 The Wild Robot – Peter Brown 🦊 Fantastic Mr Fox – Roald Dahl 🐻 The Last Bear – Hannah Gold 🦉 The Owl Who Was Afraid of the Dark – Jill Tomlinson 🍂 The Miraculous Journey of Edward Tulane – Kate DiCamillo 🌲 The Explorer – Katherine Rundell ⭐ The Little Prince – Antoine de Saint-Exupéry 🌾 Little House in the Big Woods – Laura Ingalls Wilder 🤖 The Iron Man – Ted Hughes 📚 The Boy at the Back of the Class – Onjali Q. Raúf
🍁🔎 YOUR AUTUMN READING CHALLENGE!
When you’re outside this week, become an Autumn Detective!
🟡 a yellow leaf 🟠 an orange leaf 🔴 a red leaf 🟤 a brown leaf 🌰 a conker 🍎 an apple 🍂 a leaf bigger than your hand
✏️ Now choose your favourite!
How many words can you think of to describe your favourite autumn leaf?
crunchy • golden • tiny • enormous • speckled • shiny • smooth • spiky • colourful
❤️📚 HAPPY AUTUMN READING!
Whether you’re reading a story about a mischievous squirrel, a travelling goose, a pumpkin-filled garden or an autumn forest…
there’s always another adventure waiting on the library shelves!
🍂 Happy reading, St Stephen’s! 🍂
📖 The Library Team ❤️

Library News: Loving Libraries
📚 LOVING LIBRARIES! 📚
This week in the Library, we are celebrating BOOKS, LIBRARIES and the amazing people who help stories reach children all around the world! 🌍
How far would you travel to get your favourite book?
Would you climb onto a donkey 🫏, hop on a boat 🚤, squeeze onto a bus 🚌… or even travel with an elephant 🐘?
Through our read-aloud sessions this week, we will discover some incredible travelling libraries that take books to children who live far away from traditional libraries.
We’ll meet librarians who travel across mountains, rivers and remote villages – all because they believe that every child deserves a great story! ❤️📖
🫏 REC – Biblioburro!
📖 Biblioburro – Jeanette Winter
📖 Waiting for the Biblioburro – Monica Brown
Meet Luis Soriano, a teacher and librarian from Colombia who takes books to children living in remote villages.
But Luis doesn’t have a library building…
He has two very special helpers: Alfa and Beto – his donkeys! 🫏🫏
Together they carry books to children who might otherwise find it difficult to reach a library.
Biblioburro means “library donkey” in Spanish!
🌙 The Midnight Library – Kazuno Kohara
THE MIDNIGHT LIBRARY Kazuno Kohara
A magical little library, a mysterious night-time world and plenty of books to discover!
🐭 YEAR 1 – Library Mouse
📖 Library Mouse – Daniel Kirk
Meet Sam, a little mouse who lives in a library.
Sam loves books so much that he decides to become an author himself! ✍️🐭
He secretly makes his own books and leaves them on the library shelves.
But what happens when the children want to meet the mysterious author?
Would you be brave enough to reveal your secret identity?
🐉 YEAR 2 – Libraries to the Rescue!
📖 How the Library (Not the Prince) Saved Rapunzel – Wendy Meddour
Rapunzel is waiting to be rescued…
But forget the prince!
This time, the library comes to the rescue! 📚
A funny, rhyming and clever twist on a very familiar fairy tale – with a wonderfully feisty heroine.
🐰 Wanted! Ralfy Rabbit, Book Burglar – Emily MacKenzie
Oh no! Someone has been stealing books! 😱
But who is the mysterious book burglar?
Can you solve the library mystery?
🌍 AMAZING LIBRARY FACTS
📚 FACT 1: The oldest known libraries date back thousands of years – long before computers, Kindles or even paperbacks!
🫏 FACT 2: The Biblioburro in Colombia uses donkeys to carry books to children in remote communities.
🐪 FACT 3: In some parts of the world, camels have been used as travelling libraries, carrying books across hot and remote areas.
🐘 FACT 4: There have even been library elephants! In some communities, elephants have helped transport books to children who live far from traditional libraries.
🚢 FACT 5: Books can travel by boat, bus, bicycle and even canoe to reach children in remote places.
😂 BOOK & LIBRARY JOKES
Why did the book go to the doctor? Because it had a bad spine! 😂📖
What do you call a book that tells jokes? A comic book! 😆
What did the book say to the librarian? “Can you please check me out?” 😜
Why don’t books ever get cold? Because they always have covers! 🥶📕
📚 10 BOOKS EVERY LIBRARY LOVER SHOULD DISCOVER
Here are some wonderful books for primary-aged children who love books, stories and libraries:
🐭 The Library Mouse – Daniel Kirk
🫏 Biblioburro – Jeanette Winter
🌙 The Midnight Library – Kazuno Kohara
📖 Dog Loves Books – Louise Yates
🦁 The Library Lion – Michelle Knudsen
❤️ WHAT WOULD YOUR LIBRARY LOOK LIKE?
If you could build your dream library, what would it contain?
🐉 a dragon guarding the books? 🛝 a giant slide between the shelves? 🌳 a treehouse reading corner? 🍦 an ice-cream machine? 🐱 cats curled up on the cushions? 🚀 a rocket that takes you to different worlds?
There are no limits in a library – because every book is a doorway to somewhere new! 🌎✨📚
Happy reading, everyone! ❤️

Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
St Stephen’s takes pride in the fact that it is an inclusive school where every child matters. We recognise that any child may experience additional needs at some point on their school journey and that for some children, these needs may be more long term requiring more personalised planning and support. We strive to deliver this support to the best of our ability, seeking advice from professional bodies as appropriate, ensuring staff are trained and confident to teach for a range of needs, working closely with parents and carers to enhance the learning experiences and ensuring that the child’s views are heard.

Competitive Sport
St. Stephen’s embraces competitive sport and wants as many children as possible to enjoy competing at an appropriate level. We provide all pupils with opportunities to take part in competitive sport at a level relevant to each individual. We achieve this by competing in Borough events, playing friendlies with local schools and organising a variety of intra-school competitions.
We enter as many Borough competitions as possible, as part of the School Games program. This includes competitions in football, netball, cricket, tag rugby, athletics, swimming, gymnastics, dodgeball and tennis. We enter competitive teams into these events and offer all children in the appropriate year groups the opportunity to trial for these teams. We have an excellent track record in these events, having over recent years won a number of them. Winning schools then represent the Borough in the annual London Youth Games and, as such, St Stephen’s in recent years has represented Hammersmith & Fulham at the London Youth Games in indoor athletics, Quad Kids athletics, football, tennis, cricket, netball, tag rugby, hockey kwiksticks and gymnastics. For further explanation of the School Games, please visit their website here: https://www.yourschoolgames.com/.
We want as many children as possible to play in teams so, wherever possible, we enter “B” and “C” teams into Borough competitions. Over 100 different children each year represent the school in a Borough School Games competition. In addition, we are continuing to raise the profile of sport at St Stephen’s by forming links with other schools in the area with which we play friendly matches in a variety of sports. This enables an ever increasing number of children to enjoy the benefits of representing the school in a team.
Each year all children from Years 1 – 6 take part in Sports Day at Perivale Athletics track, which sees the classes competing against each other in their Houses. By using Perivale Athletics track we are able to offer the children the experience of competing in a proper stadium environment. We also organise house tournaments throughout the year to consolidate the children’s learning in each PE unit at the end of each half term, so that they can all compete at an appropriate level, and all Key Stage 2 children play in an intra-school football tournament at our local 4G astro pitches.
Latest Success
July 2023 – Champions of the Hammersmith and Fulham Mayor’s Cup! After a tense match, our girls’ team scored the winning penalty making them champions of the borough. They all played incredibly well and thoroughly deserved the success. Well done girls!

🌳 Let’s Hug a Tree! 🌳
This week children will enjoy books and stories celebrating trees. We will talk about the importance of trees to our planet and all that they provide, from clean air to food and habitats.
We will be reading about Katherine Olivia Sessions and her job as a tree hunter in San Diego, as well as Nobel Peace Prize winner Wangari Maathai and her role in the Green Belt Movement. Below are the books each year group will enjoy in the coming week.
📚 Don’t Forget Our Writing Competitions!

🌲 Tree Facts for KS1 🌲
🌿 Fact 1: Trees help us breathe! Their leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.
🍎 Fact 2: Trees can give us food. Apples, pears, oranges, cherries and many other fruits grow on trees.
🐿️ Fact 3: Trees are homes for lots of animals. Birds can build nests in them, while squirrels, insects and other creatures can find food and shelter among their branches.

Why did the tree go to the dentist? 🌳 Because it needed a root canal! 😁
What did one tree say to another tree? 🌲 “Leaf me alone!” 🍃😂
Why are trees so good at solving problems? 🌳 Because they always branch out and think of new ideas! 🤔🌿

Residential Trips
Year 2 Swanage, Dorset
In Year 2 St Stephens offers children the opportunity to visit Dorset as part of their Humanities and Science work on ‘the seaside and habitats’. They take a boat trip to the idyllic Brownsea Island to experience island living and find out about the native red squirrels. The island is a haven for wildlife so the aim is to spot lots of wading birds and deer with binoculars at the ready! Children also explore the Jurassic Coast and find out about fossils and different types of rocks at Durlston Country Park.
For their first residential trip at St Stephen’s this trip is for a one night. The children stay at YHA Swanage, which is a large Victorian sea-facing hostel. Dinner, breakfast and lunch are provided by the hostel. The school travels to and from Dorset by coach.
Year 4 Woodrow High House
In Year 4 the children progress to a two night stay at an activities centre in Buckinghamshire. Activities are centred on physical education and bonding activities. The children participate in a range of challenges including archery, low ropes, and problem-solving. They also have the opportunity to sing songs around a campfire and throw some moves at the disco!
In Year 5, the children study World War 1 in History. After studying this topic, the children have the opportunity to immerse themselves in the WW1 battlefields on the France/Belgium border. Travelling to St Omer, the children stay in a French Chateau and travel to Ypres to visit Tyne Cot Cemetery, Langemark German Cemetery, Menin Gate and Passchendaele Museum. During this trip, the children get to explore the historic trenches and pay respects to the fallen soldiers of WW1, including an old St Stephen’s pupil. They enjoy traditional French cuisine and get a chance to visit a Belgian chocolate shop when in Ypres. This trip is rounded off with a trip Boulogne-sur-Mer, where the children follow a trail to explore the old city and finish with a visit to the beach. This trip extends the children’s historical knowledge, builds independence and encourages team building skills.
In their final year at St Stephen’s Year 6 take part in two, one week residential trips, one in Autumn term and one in Summer term.
PGL: At St Stephen’s we believe that it is very important for the whole cohort of Y6 pupils to take part and enjoy this adventurous experience. It is a hugely enriching bonding experience to kick-start the children’s final year at primary school. The activities at PGL have been carefully selected to improve the children’s knowledge, develop their skills, confidence, and independence, and will be great fun too. The children enjoy activities from abseiling and zip wire, to fencing and problem solving.
Spain: Having completed SATs, Year 6 are offered a second residential trip to further the children’s language learning experience. This trip abroad consists of a four-night full board stay in a Spanish language school in the authentic Spanish town of El Puerto de Santa Maria, near Cadiz in Andalucía. The trip includes cultural excursions (tour of Cadiz, cathedral visit, bull ring, castle) and activities (tapas making, churros eating!) and of course the all-important Spanish language lessons to support the curriculum.

Diversity in the Curriculum
At St Stephen’s, we are committed to delivering an integrated diverse curriculum across all areas of learning and experience. Our aim is to make certain that children of all backgrounds are able to see themselves and their families represented in every aspect of their education. We hold regular meetings with parents to discuss changes and improvements that have been made in this area and to take suggestions for future development. We have a dedicated parent diversity group that works alongside the teaching body to ensure representation reflective of our school and local community.
As well as diversity within the teaching curriculum, we also have a number of enrichment events every year including Arts Week, Hispanic Day and A Celebration of Black Voices Week.
As well as these, we have several theme days to raise awareness and tackle prejudice in all its forms such as Show Racism the Red Card and International Women’s Day.

Chair of Governors
The governing body of St Stephen’s has a number of responsibilities. Essentially, we work with the headteacher to help run the school. While the head is responsible for its day-to-day management, we provide oversight as a “critical friend” – to set strategic direction, review progress and both challenge and support the management team.
Governors come from a variety of different backgrounds – all are voluntary and all attend regular full meetings of the Governing Body as well as sub-committees to do with the school’s finances, staffing, premises, curriculum etc. You will recognise some of us from our pictures below as fellow parents – other governors may have no children at St Stephen’s but can still be seen at various events or on school visits. We all share in the school’s vision and values and are proud to be part of the St Stephen’s community.

Class Teacher: Miss Bill
Teaching Assistant: Miss Kayleigh

Class Updates
Friday 2nd October 2026
As always, we have been working very hard here in Year 6!
In English, the children started their work on our topic of autobiographies, reading the first part of Floella Benjamin’s life in Trinidad in preparation for their own writing. They examined how she spoke about the key events in her life, before coming up with the key features of an autobiography.
In Maths, we have been revising the four operations: starting with addition and subtraction, before moving on to multiplying 4-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers and tackling word problems. These are tricky concepts but the children are working incredibly hard to consolidate what they learnt in Year 5.
We have spent the rest of the week classifying living things in Science, which the children loved. For RE, the children have been put in groups to research a given local place of worship, which they will then present to the class, continuing our learning about how our local area has changed over the past 50 years. In History, we have continued looking at Ancient Greece, this week focussing on the two main city states: Athens and Sparta. We learnt how these two city states are different and discussed which one we would prefer to visit and why.
For Art, we studied Toyin Ojih Odutola, a Nigerian-American contemporary visual artist known for her vivid multimedia drawings and works on paper. The children used their own side profile to create their own piece taking inspiration from her unique style of complex mark-making and lavish portraits.
But it hasn’t been all lessons! On Tuesday, we held the ever-popular House Captain elections. We were so impressed with the confidence each candidate showed – standing up in front of their peers and teachers is no easy task but everyone did brilliantly. The standard of presentations was very high and we want to congratulate all who put themselves forward. Win or lose, you should all feel very proud of yourselves.
Finally, a reminder: there is now a huge focus on Times Tables, especially with the statutory Y4 test in place. Our recent work on multiplication and division has shown that some children would benefit from a bit of extra practice. While there are lots of sing-along songs aimed at younger children, Year 6 might prefer something a little more engaging. Here are some useful links to practise at home:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XT3vxohtBg
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z_BJjR9rdwA
Have a lovely weekend.
Miss Bill and Miss Marchant
Friday 25th September 2026
What a week we had last week! PGL was excellent and the children all had a fantastic time – we are sure you have already heard plenty about the wonderful activities we took part in.
In English, we have continued working on our narrative unit based on Neil Gaiman’s Wolves in the Walls. The children have been learning how to use figurative language naturally in their writing, as well as practising fronted adverbials. Yesterday, they completed their very first ‘final piece’ of Year 6 and from what we’ve read so far, the results are fantastic.
In Maths, we have been revising the four operations: starting with addition and subtraction, before moving on to recapping factors and multiples. These are tricky concepts but the children are working incredibly hard to consolidate what they learnt in Year 5. This weekend’s homework marks the start of our new White Rose Homework books. This link directly to the learning done in class so is great for practise and consolidation.
The rest of the week has been just as busy. In Science, we’ve been identifying if things are living or non-living; in RE, we learnt about how our local area has changed over the past 50 years with the special help of local resident Mrs Connor, and in History, we’ve continued our work on the Ancient Greeks, this week looking at the different types of government.
Finally, a reminder: there is now a huge focus on Times Tables, especially with the statutory Y4 test in place. Our recent work on multiplication and division has shown that some children would benefit from a bit of extra practice. While there are lots of sing-along songs aimed at younger children, Year 6 might prefer something a little more engaging. Here are some useful links to practise at home:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9&v=8QU_E0u-tP4
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e7rYbk9PNuM
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XT3vxohtBg
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z_BJjR9rdwA
Have a lovely weekend!
Miss Bill and Miss Marchant
Friday 11th September 2026
A very busy week here in Year 6, but it has been lovely to really get into teaching our first topics of the year. We are so pleased with the children’s enthusiasm and hardworking attitudes, which we are sure will continue over the year!
In English, we began our first topic which is a narrative unit using the book ‘The Wolves in the Walls’ by Neil Gaiman. The children have been looking at creating tension in their writing through using a variety of sentence starters (ISPACED), direct speech and high-level vocabulary. As the week has progressed, the children have really impressed us as they have taken on the skills taught to them to allow their writing to create tension, adding suspense for the reader.
In Maths, we started working on our place value knowledge, looking at reading and writing numbers to 10,000,000, the power of 10, rounding numbers and negative numbers before doing the end of topic test to practise everything they have learnt. After our trip, we will begin addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
In RE, we were introduced to our new topic which saw us looking at all the different faith communities in our local area. On our walks to school, we may come across a Greek Orthodox Church, the Mosque, a Catholic Church, the Uxbridge Road Tabernacle as well as several Church of England Churches. We discussed how Shepherd’s Bush is a very diverse area and there is not one set religion. We are lucky, as the diversity means we can learn from all the different groups of people.
In History, we were introduced to our new topic: Ancient Greeks. For our first lesson we looked at where we would place the Greeks on a timeline. We then looked at the different Greek civilisations and thought about the legacy that the Ancient Greeks left behind.
If you have any questions about next week’s trip, please don’t hesitate to contact one of us.
Have a lovely weekend!
Miss Bill and Miss Marchant
Friday 4th September 2026
Welcome back and welcome to Year 6! We’ve heard many stories of your summers full of exciting adventures – we hope you are well rested and ready for the new school year and your child’s final year at St Stephen’s.
So far this week, we have talked about our aspirations for the year, were introduced to our Y6 value ‘hope’, wrote a paragraph about our family heritage and discussed how having a growth mind-set will be critical to succeeding.
As you may know already, the children are expected to get their homework diaries signed every Thursday in preparation for teacher signature on a Friday, this will prepare them for next year. The children also need to read every evening (even if only a couple of pages) and this is also recorded in their homework diaries.
Finally, we will be having our house captain elections on Tuesday 29th September. Each house will have four Year 6 Captains who will help lead their houses in certain events and activities. Candidates will make a presentation on why they should be elected, which they will then present to everyone in their house. Votes from each house will then be collated. Below is a job description and a few ideas that might help (more information can be found on Google Classroom).
House Captain’s Job Description
Any speech or talk they give should be no more than five minutes.
Please feel free to email us with any queries or issues. We are looking forward to teaching your children – it is set to be a great year.
Have a lovely weekend,
Miss Bill and Miss Marchant
